title: Inside the BME280
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: A clickable cutaway of the BME280 with a seven-stage trace of one pressure reading using the real Bosch compensation formulas, and a skip-the-temperature fault that makes the reported pressure swing by over 60 hPa with no weather involved.

learningObjectives: Summarise how three separate transduction mechanisms coexist on one chip.
Explain why the temperature element is required even by a program that only wants pressure.
Describe the role of the factory calibration registers.
Recognise temperature-driven pressure drift as a software fault rather than a hardware failure.
prerequisites: Chapters 6, 7 and 8: temperature, pressure and humidity sensing

keyQuestions: How do three different sensing mechanisms fit in a package 2.5 mm across?
Why can a raw ADC count not be reported as a pressure?
Why does a pressure-only program still have to read the temperature?
If your pressure readings drift with the room, what would you check first?
commonMisconceptions: Each sensing element has its own ADC.
Calibration constants are the same for every chip of this model.
Raw counts are already a physical measurement.
Pressure drifting with room temperature means the sensor has failed.
assessmentOpportunities: Names each block and connects it to the chapter that taught its mechanism.
Records the trace values and identifies where units first appear.
Plots reported pressure against ambient temperature with the fault on and explains the slope.
